recent_posts.title: Hashtag Jakarta EE #331
recent_posts.summary: Issue 331 of the Hashtag Jakarta EE newsletter covers the author's participation in the ShiftAPPens 2026 hackathon in Coimbra, Portugal, where Jakarta EE sponsored a student challenge. It highlights an analyst report from ECI positioning Jakarta EE as built for longevity and vendor-neutral enterprise integration. Updates on Jakarta EE 12 Milestone 4 are shared, with expected deliverables including REST 5.0, CDI 5.0, JSON-P 2.2, and JSON-B 3.1. The author also previews an upcoming talk at JavaConnect KE 2026 in Nairobi on augmenting LLMs with agentic techniques using Jakarta EE.

recent_posts.title: Hashtag Jakarta EE #330
recent_posts.summary: Issue #330 of the Hashtag Jakarta EE newsletter covers the author's attendance at Open Community eXperience (OCX) in Brussels, the Eclipse Foundation rolling out GitHub Copilot Enterprise to committers for automating Jakarta EE Specification Process tasks, and a recommended article on API versioning in Java using JAX-RS with Jakarta EE and MicroProfile.

recent_posts.title: adam bien's blog
recent_posts.summary: Episode 145 of airhacks.tv covers a range of Java 25 and architecture topics: the BCE (Boundary-Control-Entity) pattern from 1992 applied to modern package structure, a zero-dependency MCP server, Agent Smith — a ~130KB zero-dependency Java 25 agent framework with episodic memory and delegation, GPU-accelerated local LLM execution via TornadoVM with Apple Metal support for Mistral and DevStral, and the Z ecosystem of zero-dependency Java 25 scripts including ZUnit (a ~300-line parallel test runner) and ZB build tool. The episode also touches on LLMs understanding standards better than frameworks for lean code generation, and upcoming AirHacks Live workshops on spec-driven Java development.

recent_posts.title: Hashtag Jakarta EE #329
recent_posts.summary: Issue 329 of the Hashtag Jakarta EE newsletter covers the upcoming Open Community eXperience 2026 conference in Brussels and provides a detailed milestone timeline for the Jakarta EE 12 release. recent_posts.title: UserRegistry Attribute Reader Enhancement and Jandex Index Format Support Update in 26.0.0.3- OpenLiberty.io
recent_posts.summary: Open Liberty 26.0.0.3 ships two notable enhancements. First, the UserRegistry API gains two new methods — getAttributesForUser() and getUsersByAttribute() — enabling applications to retrieve specific user attributes (e.g., email, phone number) and search for users by attribute values from LDAP and custom registries, capabilities previously only available via the WebSphere VMM API. Second, Open Liberty now supports Jandex index formats 11–13 (generated by Jandex 3.1.0 through 3.5.3), removing the previous cap at format 10. This allows developers to use the latest Jandex Maven and Gradle plugins without workarounds, preserving annotation-indexing startup performance benefits. No server.xml changes are required; Jandex support is enabled via the useJandex property. Notable limitations include the mpGraphQL feature remaining capped at format 10, and the requirement to keep Jandex indexes synchronized with application classes.
